title: Cardiac Electrophysiological Impact of Sodium Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors: A Comprehensive Review.
summary: SGLT2i (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors) reduce heart failure hospitalizations, cardiovascular death, and certain arrhythmic events beyond glycemic control. However, their specific effects on cardiac autonomic function and arrhythmogenesis, as well as the potential involvement of microRNAs in mediating these benefits, remain incompletely understood. This review synthesizes clinical and preclinical evidence on the impact of SGLT2i on cardiac autonomic regulation and arrhythmias, emphasizing the interplay between SGLT2i, microRNA expression, and cardiovascular risk. We conducted a comprehensive literature search for clinical trials, meta-analyses, observational studies, and preclinical investigations. Outcomes included heart rate variability, heart rate turbulence, atrial/ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Studies examining microRNA profiles associated with SGLT2i treatment and their links to cardiac fibrosis, inflammation, and arrhythmogenic substrates were analyzed in depth. Clinical evidence indicates that SGLT2i improve cardiac autonomic balance by reducing sympathetic overactivity and enhancing parasympathetic tone in patients with type 2 diabetes and cardiac autonomic neuropathy. Meta-analyses and post hoc data from cardiovascular outcome trials suggest a modest but consistent reduction in atrial fibrillation/flutter and, in some cohorts, sudden cardiac death, potentially reflecting sympathoinhibition, improved hemodynamics, and modulation of myocardial ion homeostasis. Preclinical studies support anti-arrhythmic properties through sodium-hydrogen exchanger inhibition, late sodium current suppression, and metabolic shift towards ketone utilization. SGLT2i modulate several key microRNAs implicated in heart failure and arrhythmic risk, including miR-21, miR-29, miR-30, miR-34a, and miR-92, which may partly underlie the attenuation of arrhythmogenic substrates and improved autonomic regulation. SGLT2i favorably affect cardiac autonomic function and reduce the burden of certain arrhythmias, potentially through modulation of disease-associated microRNAs. Integrating clinical autonomic outcomes with microRNA profiling provides mechanistic insights into their cardioprotective actions. Dedicated trials are warranted to clarify causality, dose-dependency, and the therapeutic potential of microRNA-SGLT2i interactions for arrhythmia prevention and management in high-risk populations.

title: Multimodality Imaging for Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Practical Guidance Across Preprocedural, Intraprocedural, and Postprocedural Phases.
authors: Left Atrial Appendage International Working Group
summary: Left atrial appendage closure is an increasingly used stroke prevention therapy for patients with atrial fibrillation who are unable to maintain long-term anticoagulation. Imaging quality and consistency are central to procedural safety and long-term outcomes, yet practice varies widely across centers. This review presents a practical, phase-based multimodality imaging framework intended to provide guidance and minimum standards for image acquisition and interpretation across all phases of left atrial appendage closure care, including preprocedural planning and thrombus exclusion, intraprocedural guidance and complication detection, and postprocedural surveillance for device-related thrombus and peridevice leak. Because sizing rules, sealing mechanisms, and leak patterns differ between the 2 contemporary platforms, device-specific considerations for the Watchman and Amulet systems are addressed throughout. Transesophageal echocardiography remains the reference standard for thrombus detection and procedural guidance, while cardiac computed tomography offers high spatial resolution, detailed 3-dimensional characterization, and complementary leak assessment, with optimal modality selection influenced by patient characteristics, operator expertise, and institutional resources. Intracardiac echocardiography and mini transesophageal echocardiographic support anesthesia-sparing workflows. Standardized device-related thrombus and peridevice leak classification and harmonized imaging protocols can enhance reproducibility and facilitate cross-center comparisons. Emerging technologies including computed tomography first workflows, 4-dimensional imaging, AI applications, and computational modeling further advance precision planning and surveillance.

title: Retraction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Effectiveness of Intravenous Magnesium Sulphate in the Treatment of Acute Fast Atrial Fibrillation in Non-surgical Adult Patients.
Renal Function and 4-Year Outcomes in Edoxaban-Treated Patients: A Sub-Analysis From the ETNA-AF Europe Study.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants, like edoxaban, are essential in managing atrial fibrillation (AF). The impact of renal function on edoxaban dosages in real-world settings remains unclear. This 4-year ETNA-AF-Europe study follow-up analysis investigated how chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages affect the safety and effectiveness of usual edoxaban doses.

METHODS: ETNA-AF-Europe (NCT02944019) was an observational study conducted from 2016 to 2022 across 776 centres in 10 European countries. Hazard ratios (HR) and annualized event rates were calculated for all-cause death, cardiovascular (CV) death, stroke and bleeding events for the overall population and participants stratified by dose (30/60 mg) and CKD stages at baseline.

RESULTS: Of the 13,164 participants in the full analysis set, 9114 participants with CKD (Stage 1, n = 2064; Stage 2, n = 4855; Stage 3, n = 1985; Stage 4, n = 135; missing, n = 75) received label-recommended edoxaban doses. Compared with CKD Stage 1, higher CKD stages were associated with increased risks for stroke (Stage 3: HR [95% CI]: 1.889 [1.240-2.878], p = 0.003) and CV death (HR [95% CI]; Stage 4: 14.450 [8.270-25.247], Stage 3: 4.672 [3.312-6.969], Stage 2: 2.066 [1.394-3.062], all p < 0.001). All-cause death followed a similar trend. After adjusting for age, sex, body weight, CHA2DS2-VASc and modified HAS-BLED scores, most bleeding and effectiveness outcomes showed no nominally significant differences across CKD stages.

CONCLUSIONS: Edoxaban in patients with AF is effective and well tolerated across CKD stages and appropriate label dosing can offset the risk from renal impairment.

title: Factors associated with short- and long-term maintenance of sinus rhythm after successful elective electrical cardioversion.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Electrical cardioversion (ECV) effectively restores sinus rhythm in patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) and atrial flutter (AFL), although arrhythmia recurrence is common. We aimed to identify factors associated with a higher probability of maintaining sinus rhythm one month after successful ECV, and after one year in those who were arrhythmia-free after the first month.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included patients who underwent elective ECV for persistent AF or AFL between January 2011 and June 2023. Clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic characteristics were analyzed to identify parameters associated with the maintenance of sinus rhythm.

RESULTS: We included 297 ECV procedures. ECV was successful in 91.9% of patients and sinus rhythm was maintained in 89.7% of them at one month and in 40.3% at one year follow-up. Shorter arrhythmia duration (OR = 0.863, 95% CI: 0.76-0.98, p = 0.026) and ventricular pacing on the pre-procedural ECG (OR = 5.212, 95% CI: 1.16-23.48, p = 0.032) were associated with one-month success. Factors associated with one-year sinus rhythm maintenance in patients who were in sinus rhythm during monthly follow-up were smaller left atrial dimensions (OR = 0.817, 95%CI: 0.77-0.98, p = 0.022), the first-ever arrhythmia episode (OR = 3.320, 95%CI: 1.10-10.05, p = 0.034), lower CHA2DS2-VASc score (OR = 0.132, 95%CI: 0.03-0.54, p = 0.005), non-smoking status (OR = 0.120, 95%CI: 0.04-0.37, p < 0.001), no previous ECV (OR = 0.082, 95%CI: 0.01-0.47, p = 0.005), and antiarrhythmic therapy (OR = 2.486, 95%CI: 1.01-8.65, p = 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: ECV is a reasonable rhythm-control strategy in AF/AFL particularly when performed early after arrhythmia onset, in non-smokers and patients with fewer comorbidities, antiarrhythmic treatment, smaller left atrium and no prior ECV.

title: Massive Mediastinal Hematoma After Reablation for Atrial Fibrillation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Mediastinal hematoma is a rare but severe complication of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. We present a case of a massive mediastinal hematoma following reablation for AF in a patient with a history of cardiac surgery.

CASE SUMMARY: A 70-year-old woman with rheumatic heart disease, prosthetic aortic and mitral valves, and mild thalassemia underwent catheter ablation for recurrent AF. She developed acute dyspnea and orthopnea 30 hours after the procedure. Computed tomography angiography revealed a 69.2 mm × 51.1 mm hematoma, compressing the left atrium. Conservative management was initiated, including blood transfusion and diuretics. The patient's symptoms improved within 2 days, and subsequent imaging demonstrated complete resolution of the hematoma at 12-month follow-up.

DISCUSSION: The occurrence of the massive hematoma could be attributed to preexisting atrial fibrosis and pericardial adhesions from prior cardiac surgery, potential vascular fragility and platelet dysfunction because of thalassemia, challenges in accessing the scarred atrial septum, thermal injury to the left atrial roof, and the perioperative hemodynamic changes.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: For patients with a history of cardiac surgery and thalassemia, vigilance for mediastinal hematoma is essential following catheter ablation procedures.

title: Anatomical Insight Into Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Papillary Muscles.
summary: The papillary muscles (PAMs) are important sites of origin of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs). Although catheter ablation of idiopathic PAM VAs has proven to be an effective treatment, these arrhythmias remain challenging compared with other idiopathic VAs despite advances in technologies and techniques. This is related to the unique anatomical challenges of these structures. PAMs are anatomically unique in their location, morphology, histologic composition, and connections with surrounding structures. Electrophysiological studies and catheter ablation of PAM VAs have revealed specific electrocardiographic and electrophysiological characteristics of idiopathic PAM VAs, such as inconsistent precordial transition, discordant QRS axis, multiform VA morphologies, and preferential conduction. Anatomical studies with the aid of imaging modalities, such as intracardiac echocardiography, computed tomography, and cardiac magnetic resonance, have helped define the anatomical background underlying these electrocardiographic and electrophysiological characteristics. This article reviews the unique anatomy of PAMs from an electrophysiological standpoint to better understand the anatomy of the PAMs and thereby improve the outcomes of catheter ablation of idiopathic PAM VAs.

title: Pilot safety and efficacy trial of amiodarone-infused biologic acellular biatrial patches to prevent new-onset postoperative atrial fibrillation.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: New onset postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) occurs in approximately 25% to 40% of patients undergoing heart surgery and is associated with increased perioperative morbidity and mortality. We evaluated the safety and exploratory efficacy of amiodarone-infused CardiaMend (Helios Cardio) biatrial patches for POAF prevention.

METHODS: A single-center pilot clinical trial enrolled 40 patients after applying inclusions and exclusion criteria, randomized in 1:1 fashion. Patients in the treatment group received the CardiaMend patch, a porous acellular matrix derived from fetal bovine dermis, infused with 70 mg amiodarone, placed on both atria, whereas the control group received standard care. The primary end point was safety, defined as major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Secondary end points included POAF, length of hospital stay, 30-day readmission, and POAF duration.

RESULTS: The 2 randomized groups had similar baseline characteristics. There were 2 major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events: 1 patient in the control group experienced an embolic stroke with full recovery before discharge, and 1 patient in the treatment group died from an acute abdominal event following intra-aortic balloon pump removal, deemed unrelated to the study device. The incidence of POAF (4 patients [20%] vs 8 patients [40%]; P = .30) and mean atrial fibrillation duration (2.5 ± 2.4 days vs 3.8 ± 4.1 days) were lower in the treatment group. Mean length of hospital stay was shorter in the treatment group (5.8 ± 1.2 days vs 9.3 ± 7.5 days; P = .07). At 30-day follow-up, Holter monitoring revealed no atrial fibrillation in the treatment group and 3 (15%) patients in the control group (P = .23), and readmission rates were also lower in the treatment group (5% vs 15%; P = .6).

CONCLUSIONS: This pilot randomized clinical trial showed that amiodarone-infused CardiaMend biatrial patches were safe, with no evidence of systemic amiodarone toxicity. Treatment with amiodarone-infused CardiaMend patches was associated with a clinically noticeable reduction in POAF, length of stay, and postdischarge atrial fibrillation.

title: Minimally invasive mitral surgery in patients with high pulmonary artery pressure: Results of a multicenter observational study.
authors: Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Surgery Registry Investigators
summary:
OBJECTIVES: Pulmonary hypertension is diagnosed in 40% to 75% of patients affected by mitral valve diseases. Little is known regarding outcomes of patients with pulmonary hypertension undergoing mitral valve oeprations through minimally invasive approaches. This study compares the characteristics and in-hospital outcomes of patients undergoing minimally invasive mitral valve surgery, stratified by systolic pulmonary artery pressure.

METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective, prospective, observational study included adults undergoing mitral valve operations through a right minithoracotomy with or without tricuspid valve surgery and atrial fibrillation ablation between 2020 and 2024. Comparisons were performed between patients with systolic pulmonary artery pressure less than 31 mm Hg, systolic pulmonary artery pressure 31 to 55 mm Hg, and systolic pulmonary artery pressure more than 55 mm Hg based on European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II cutoffs for systolic pulmonary artery pressure categories.

RESULTS: This analysis included 1121 patients (female, 47.5%; median age, 69 years, interquartile range, 59-77). Median systolic pulmonary artery pressure was 38 mm Hg (interquartile range, 30-50; systolic pulmonary artery pressure <31 mm Hg: n = 307, 27.4%; systolic pulmonary artery pressure 31-55 mm Hg: n = 152, 55.3%; systolic pulmonary artery pressure >55 mm Hg: n = 194, 17.3%). Patients with higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure were older, mainly female, and characterized by more comorbidities including atrial fibrillation and renal disease. A critical perioperative state was diagnosed in 12% of patients with systolic pulmonary artery pressure more than 55 mm Hg (P < .001). Patients with higher systolic pulmonary artery pressure more frequently underwent mitral valve replacement and tricuspid annuloplasty and experienced more postoperative dialysis and pacemaker implantation but comparable rates of conversions to sternotomy, respiratory and bleeding complications, and in-hospital mortality (systolic pulmonary artery pressure <31 mm Hg: n = 3, 1%; systolic pulmonary artery pressure 31-55 mm Hg: n = 6, 1%; systolic pulmonary artery pressure >55 mm Hg: n = 5, 2.6%; P = .222) compared with patients with lower systolic pulmonary artery pressure.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite a higher preoperative complexity, patients with high systolic pulmonary artery pressure could be considered for minimally invasive mitral valve surgery with acceptable rates of major intraoperative or postoperative complications regardless of their systolic pulmonary artery pressure values.

title: Pericardial fluid cardiac troponin I predicts postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: Cardiac troponin I (cTnI) is a sensitive biomarker of myocardial injury. We hypothesized that cTnI measured in pericardial drainage fluid (PCF), which reflects the cardiac microenvironment, may enhance risk stratification for postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) after coronary artery bypass grafting.

METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 114 patients undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting were enrolled. The primary end point was new-onset POAF within 7 days postoperatively. Blood and PCF cTnI at 6 hours postoperatively were measured. Variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and were then incorporated into multivariable logistic regression to construct a predictive model. A simplified risk score (CALT score) was developed. Model performance was compared with existing POAF tools, including the POAF score, CHA2DS2-VASc, and the atrial fibrillation risk index.

RESULTS: POAF occurred in 30.7% of the cohort. Postoperative 6-hour PCF-cTnI was an independent predictor of POAF (odds ratio, 5.502; 95% CI, 1.887-16.045; P = .002) and significantly enhanced continuous net reclassification improvement (0.562; 95% CI, 0.189-0.921; P = .002). The CALT score comprised left circumflex artery lesions, left atrial diameter, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, postoperative 0-hour serum calcium, and postoperative 6-hour PCF-cTnI. The PCF-cTnI-based model demonstrated good discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.821), with favorable calibration and clinical utility. Compared with commonly used risk scores, the CALT score exhibited superior discrimination and calibration.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides novel evidence that PCF-cTnI is a strong predictor of POAF. The CALT score, integrating PCF-cTnI with clinical factors, provided superior predictive performance by capturing both the vulnerable atrial substrate and localized myocardial injury.

title: Coronary sinus lactate at reperfusion: A predictor of atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting.
summary:
OBJECTIVE: Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is the most common complication after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). This study explored the association of coronary sinus (CS) lactate levels with POAF after CABG.

METHODS: This was a single-center prospective cohort study of patients without a history of atrial fibrillation undergoing isolated CABG (December 2024 to February 2026). CS lactate was sampled before initiation of cardiopulmonary bypass (pre-CPB), before cross-clamp removal (pre-XC), and after cross-clamp removal (post-XC). POAF was defined as electrocardiogram-documented atrial fibrillation treated with amiodarone during the index hospitalization. Restricted cubic splines were used to define a binary cutoff of post-XC CS lactate at >3 mmol/L. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to assess the association between CS lactate elevation and POAF.

RESULTS: Of the 94 patients included, POAF occurred in 24 patients (26%). Patients with POAF were older and more commonly male but had similar median CPB time and XC duration. Patients with a post-XC lactate >3 mmol/L (n = 13/94, 14%) had significantly greater rates of POAF compared with those without lactate elevation (62% vs 20%, P = .001). After risk adjustment, post-XC lactate >3 mmol/L was associated with a 11.7-fold increase in odds of POAF (P = .010). Increasing age was also linked to greater likelihood of POAF. There was no significant association of POAF with CPB time, XC duration, pre-CPB CS lactate, or pre-XC CS lactate.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated CS lactate after cardiac reperfusion was associated with increased likelihood of POAF. Our findings suggest that CS lactate may be used to guide POAF prophylaxis.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Versus Oral Anticoagulation in Atrial Fibrillation: A Comprehensive Evidence Synthesis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulation (OAC) remains the cornerstone of stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) but is limited by bleeding risk. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) devices offer an alternative; however, recent randomized trials have reported inconsistent efficacy compared with OAC.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing LAAO with OAC through April 1, 2026, using MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible studies enrolled adults (≥18 years) with AF randomized to LAAO or OAC. Primary and secondary outcomes were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Individual patient-level data (IPD) were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves for time-to-event sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Six RCTs (n = 7,004; mean age 72 years; CHA2DS2‑VASc 3.9; HAS‑BLED 1.7; mean follow-up 38 months) were included. LAAO showed no significant difference in ischemic stroke (RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.82-1.76), major bleeding (RR 0.77, 95% CI 0.50-1.17), or all-cause mortality (RR 0.96, 95% CI 0.82-1.13) compared with OAC. Hemorrhagic stroke risk was significantly lower with LAAO (RR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.93). Reconstructed IPD demonstrated similar stroke and bleeding risks (HR 1.24 and 0.84, respectively) but lower all-cause mortality with LAAO (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.95).

CONCLUSION: LAAO provides comparable ischemic stroke prevention and major bleeding outcomes to OAC and reduces hemorrhagic stroke risk. Reconstructed IPD analyses suggest a possible mortality benefit that warrants further investigation. Future studies using contemporary devices and post-ablation populations are needed to refine patient selection and further characterize the comparative clinical outcomes of LAAO and OAC in AF patients.

title: Temporary Active Fixation Leads in Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Patients With Baseline Right Bundle Branch Block.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Patients with pre-existing right bundle branch block (RBBB) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) are at a high risk of complete heart block, often requiring prolonged temporary pacing. Conventional temporary pacing leads are associated with lead dislodgement, immobilization, and intensive care unit (ICU) monitoring. The objective of this study was to compare screw-in versus conventional temporary pacing leads after TAVR in patients with pre-existing RBBB.

METHODS: This multicenter observational study included consecutive patients with pre-existing RBBB undergoing TAVR between 2018 and 2024. Patients receiving left ventricular pacing or no postprocedural temporary pacing were excluded. Outcomes included procedural complications, ICU utilization, hospital stay, permanent pacemaker implantation, and 30-day clinical events.

RESULTS: Among 544 patients, 124 received a screw-in lead and 420 a conventional lead. Screw-in leads were associated with significantly lower ICU utilization after TAVR (23% vs. 99%, p < 0.001). Despite longer temporary pacing duration (2.4 ± 1.4 days vs. 1.2 ± 1.6 days, p < 0.001), lead dislodgement was infrequent and numerically lower with screw-in leads (0.8% vs. 3.3%). Rates of major vascular complications, bleeding, tamponade, and atrial fibrillation were similar between groups. At 30 days, permanent pacemaker implantation rates were comparable (50.0% vs. 46.2%; p = 0.455), whereas hospital stay was shorter with screw-in leads (5.2 ± 4.2 days vs. 7.4 ± 7.8 days, p < 0.001). Mortality and major adverse events were similar.

CONCLUSIONS: In TAVR recipients with pre-existing RBBB, screw-in temporary pacing leads were associated with reduced ICU utilization and shorter hospitalization without increasing complications or adverse outcomes, supporting their use for prolonged postprocedural monitoring.

title: The role of vascular resistance on coronary perfusion: differences between healthy and anomalous coronary origin under rest and exercise conditions.
summary: Sudden cardiac death (SCD) is a leading cause of mortality in young athletes and is frequently linked to congenital anomalies of the coronary arteries, particularly the anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the right sinus of Valsalva (AOLRS). Despite extensive research, the underlying mechanism remains unclear-especially in cases without structural cardiac abnormalities. In our previous studies, we identified abnormal coronary wave dynamics ("wave pathology") as a potential factor impairing perfusion in such anomalies. Building on these findings, the present study investigates the hemodynamic consequences of changes in distal coronary resistance in normal and anomalous coronary anatomies. Two in-vitro anatomical models-a normal configuration and an AOLRS model with an intramural aortic segment-were tested under rest and exercise conditions in a physiological simulator. By independently varying distal coronary resistances as an experimental representation of distal vasodilation, we observed that decreasing resistance increased flow in the manipulated coronary branch and was accompanied by a modest reduction in mean aortic pressure. In a separate set of tests, decreasing mean aortic pressure while maintaining the coronary resistance settings reduced both LCA and RCA flow, with a stronger pressure-flow dependence during exercise. These results identify a coupling between distal resistance, aortic pressure, and coronary perfusion whose effect becomes more important during exercise. In the anomalous model, this mechanism acts in a coronary circulation in which altered wave propagation and reflection were previously observed, and may add to the hemodynamic vulnerability associated with AOLRS. Its contribution to exercise-induced ischemia and SCD remains to be established.

title: Ventricular False Tendons and Ventricular Arrhythmias: Distinguishing Incidental Findings From Culprit Substrates.
summary: Ventricular false tendons are fibrous or fibromuscular cords that cross the ventricular cavity. Some contain Purkinje tissue and have been implicated in premature ventricular complexes, left posterior fascicular ventricular tachycardia, and, rarely, ventricular fibrillation. However, false tendons are also common in healthy hearts, so their visibility does not establish causality. This narrative review critically appraises the evidence and addresses three unresolved mechanistic questions. First, it is unclear whether a posteroseptal tendon forms the circuit of fascicular tachycardia or carries part of the adjacent Purkinje network. Control data are lacking, and ablation lesions involve both structures. Second, the slow, decremental, and verapamil-sensitive conduction of the P1 pathway may reflect abnormal Purkinje tissue, reduced electrical coupling, or mixed tissue composition. Third, successful ablation sites cluster at tendon insertions. We propose a junctional hypothesis in which the insertion, where a thin Purkinje-containing cord must depolarize a large myocardial mass, may form an arrhythmogenic interface. This model is untested but may account for insertion-based targets, verapamil sensitivity, and exit shifts. We also propose a graded framework that classifies a tendon as an unlikely, possible, probable, or definite culprit. A definite grade requires concordant anatomical, electrical, imaging, and procedural evidence plus at least one observation that separates the tendon from adjacent tissue. By these criteria, most reported culprit tendons are probable rather than definite. A false tendon is best regarded as a visible segment of the Purkinje network whose arrhythmogenic potential may depend on how and where it couples to the myocardium.

title: Outcomes of Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillators in Patients Being Considered for Heart Transplantation: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: Subcutaneous implantable cardioverter defibrillators (S-ICD) are an alternative to transvenous devices (TV-ICD) in patients not requiring bradycardia pacing, resynchronization (CRT) or anti-tachycardia pacing (ATP). At our center, S-ICDs are often preferred in patients being considered for heart transplantation (HTx) without pacing/CRT/ATP needs, as their removal post-HTx avoids retained transvenous leads which can preclude MRI surveillance for graft rejection. We assessed outcomes of S-ICDs in this population.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 201 S-ICD implants at our center; July 2016 - March 2025.

RESULTS: We identified 33 patients (22 male; age 46 ± 13 years) who, at time of S-ICD implant, had been referred for HTx evaluation or were referred at any time thereafter. Etiologies were nonischemic cardiomyopathy (n = 18), hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (n = 5), ischemic cardiomyopathy (n = 4), congenital heart disease (n = 4), and myocarditis (n = 2). Median follow-up was 296 days [IQR = 72-798]. Two patients died, both non-arrhythmic. Four patients received appropriate S-ICD therapies and three had inappropriate shocks due to P- or T-wave oversensing (TWOS) (n = 2), or a rapidly conducted atrial arrhythmia (n = 1). Three patients, all with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, received transvenous device upgrades: one to CRT-P for disease progression, one to TV-ICD for ATP-terminable ventricular tachycardia and one to TV-ICD due to inappropriate shocks from TWOS. Thirteen patients underwent HTx at median 257 days [IQR = 130-453] post S-ICD; three of whom were bridged with HeartMate 3 LVADs. One LVAD patient needed S-ICD deactivation due to electromagnetic interference. There were no retained device components following HTx and S-ICD extraction.

CONCLUSION: In selected pre-HTx patients, S-ICDs offer arrhythmic protection while avoiding retained leads post-HTx.

title: Long-term variability of the blood pressure components and risk of mortality events and sudden cardiac death: a prospective cohort study (2002-2020).
summary:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: To evaluate the association between variability in systolic blood pressure (SBPV), diastolic blood pressure (DBPV), mean arterial pressure (MAPV), pulse pressure (PPV), and the risk of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality (CV mortality), and sudden cardiac death (SCD) in general population.

METHODS AND RESULTS: As many as 8479 participants (5425 women; mean age 49.0 years) underwent three visits between 2002 and 2011 at three-year intervals, then were followed up until 2020. Variability of the blood pressure components was assessed using standard deviation (SD) method. Underlying causes of mortality events were adjudicated by the outcome committee. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were applied and adjusted for a comprehensive set of confounders, including mean BP values and prevalent cardiovascular disease. During a median of 10.1 years, 681, 223, and 145 events of all-cause mortality, CV mortality, and SCD with incidence rates of 8.46, 2.77, and 1.80 per 1000 person-years occurred, respectively. In multivariable-adjusted analyses, hazard ratios (95% confidence intervals) for the association between 1-SD increase in SBPV, DBPV, MAPV, and PPV and all-cause mortality were calculated as 1.08 (1.02-1.15), 1.12 (1.05-1.20), 1.12 (1.05-1.19), 1.05 (0.99-1.11); for CV mortality were 1.15 (1.04-1.28), 1.17 (1.05-1.30), 1.18 (1.06-1.31), 1.12 (1.02-1.23); regarding SCD were 1.10 (0.96-1.25), 1.16 (1.01-1.33), 1.13 (0.98-1.29), and 1.10 (0.98-1.25), respectively. Compared to participants with low-SBPV/low-DBPV, their counterparts with high-SBPV/high-DBPV had 43% and 49% significantly higher risk of all-cause- and CV mortality, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher SBP and DBP variability, independent of their mean values, was associated with mortality events, and the latter increased the risk of SCD.

title: Anxiety and depressive symptoms decline during 12-month follow-up after cardiac resynchronization therapy implantation.
Cardiac Arrest After Deceased Donor Kidney Transplant.
summary:
CASE SUMMARY: A 54-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease and a dual-chamber pacemaker for high-grade atrioventricular block underwent deceased donor kidney transplantation. Her postoperative course was complicated by marked QT prolongation and recurrent torsades de pointes (TdP), resulting in cardiac arrest. Postarrest electrocardiogram demonstrated macroscopic T-wave alternans-a rare manifestation of severe QT prolongation. Treatment with intravenous magnesium and reprogramming her pacemaker to a lower rate limit of 100 beats/min resulted in electrical stability and improvement of the QT interval.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This case underscores recognition of macroscopic T-wave alternans as a harbinger of impending TdP, vigilant QT monitoring, and evidence-based TdP management.

title: Severe Atrial Compression Detected During Electroanatomical Mapping.
Sudden Cardiac Death as the First Manifestation of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy in a Young Female Athlete: Postmortem Morphologic Diagnosis.
summary: We report a case of sudden cardiac death in a previously healthy 29-year-old female tennis player who collapsed during a family gathering with no prior cardiovascular symptoms and an unknown family history of sudden death or structural heart disease. A complete autopsy with histopathologic examination revealed a dilated right ventricle with wall thinning to 3 mm and focal transmural replacement of the myocardium by adipose tissue. Microscopically, the right ventricular wall consisted predominantly of adipose tissue, with small residual islands of hypertrophic cardiomyocytes, fibrosis, and sparse inflammatory infiltrates. A lateral left ventricular wall thickness of 15 mm, together with subepicardial fatty infiltration, prompted careful differential diagnostic consideration of athletic remodeling, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and biventricular or left-dominant phenotypes of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. Toxicologic analysis was negative. The postmortem gross and histopathologic findings fulfilled major morphologic and histologic criteria and were highly consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy; however, in the absence of premortem imaging, electrocardiographic, and genetic data, this should be regarded as a postmortem morphologic diagnosis rather than a complete multiparametric diagnosis. This case underscores the diagnostic value of systematic autopsy and histopathologic examination following sudden unexplained death in young athletes, the importance of cautious interpretation of concomitant left ventricular findings, and the need for cardiovascular and genetic evaluation of first-degree relatives.

title: Revisiting the Ischemic Cascade Using the Lens of Generative Artificial Intelligence.
